issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect PersonService.addParent(Person, Person) to return a Person (the persisted/updated person). The template declares addParent returning Person and the REST layer (PersonResource) and tests invoke and assign its return value. However, the solution repository's PersonService declares addParent as void while PersonResource and tests still call and assign its return value. This is a structural mismatch that will cause compilation errors and contradicts the specified behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's PersonService.addParent(Person, Person) signature match the template/problem by returning a Person. Specifically, change the method to return the persisted Person (e.g., return personRepository.save(person);) so that PersonResource and tests that expect and assign the return value compile and behave as specified. Ensure the method throws ResponseStatusException on invalid conditions as described.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template indicate that the service method addParent(Person person, Person parent) should return the saved/updated Person (the problem text explicitly says "addParent ... should return the result of this method call" and the template declares the method with return type Person). However, the solution implementation declares addParent(...) with return type void. This creates a conceptual/signature mismatch: callers in the template (PersonResource) and the solution tests expect a returned Person (they assign the result of personService.addParent(...)), but the solution's service method does not return anything. Students will be confused about the expected behavior and return contract of addParent and may face compilation/test failures or be uncertain which artifact to follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature and behavior across artifacts. Prefer matching the problem statement and template: change the solution's addParent method to return Person and return personRepository.save(person) (i.e., public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent) { ... person.getParents().add(parent); return personRepository.save(person); }). Alternatively, update callers (PersonResource and tests) to not expect a return value — but the first option preserves the documented contract and minimizes confusion.
